title: Ops capitalization runway spline and price-lag analysis
body:
Purpose:
Quick working model for ops capitalization (runway) where hiring cadence, deferred comp, and a delayed pricing pass ('price-lag') interact. Goal is to produce 18-month visibility and trigger points for hiring slowdowns or price nudges.

Executive summary:
- Running a spline-based runway model to smooth noisy monthly revenue and cost inputs; better reflects hiring lags and capitalization smoothing vs simple step models.
- Primary shock vector: 3%–20% token-price compression (market) realized with 3-month lag from detection to effective price changes (contract/market negotiation lag).
- Preliminary finding: with current burn and hiring plan, a sustained 8% price compression realized after 3 months would force hiring slowdowns across Product and SRE within one quarter; 15% compression requires emergency measures (credit line, pause non-critical hiring).

Assumptions (tickets/notes inline):
- Baseline revenue growth: 6% q/q ARR add from new customers; modeled monthly as 2% compounding (conservative).
- Hosted API variable cost: $0.000012 per token (weighted). Dedicated/Private margins modeled separately in separate tab (not in this sheet).
- Headcount average fully-loaded cost by tier: IC-1 $150k, IC-3 $210k, Eng-Manager $240k, Sales-Manager $220k, Ops $180k. Hiring ramp follows Q3 hiring freeze until Sep 2026 then phased rehire.
- Capitalization rule: new infra hires capitalized over 6 months, others expensed immediately.
- Price-lag: when market index (external pricing benchmark) moves, we assume contractual repricing takes effect after an operational lag of 90 days by default (configurable).

Pricing sensitivity with lag (three scenarios):
- Scenario L (Low): 3% sustained price compression realized after 3 months. Impact: reduces variable revenue 2.6% (mix-adjusted) -> small hit to gross margin, runway shrinks by ~3 weeks.
- Scenario M (Medium): 8% sustained compression realized after 3 months. Impact: revenue down ~7% -> forces targeted hiring pause and acceleration of quantization/cost-reduction playbook; runway shortens by ~8–10 weeks.
- Scenario H (High): 15% sustained compression realized after 3 months. Impact: revenue down ~13% -> immediate exec decision: extend credit line, defer $2.5M planned infra purchases, and institute hiring moratorium across non-customerfacing teams; runway negative if no action within 1 month.

Price-lag sensitivity note: because price changes take effect with contract lead times and billing cycles, the actual cash impact is smoothed: roughly 30–120 days depending on contract cohort. The spline model accounts for cohort-weighted realization curves.

Notes to self (rough):

- Consider linking this sheet to product feature launch calendar (slower launches reduce near-term revenue).
- Slack thread: #finance-runway (see conversation id FIN-RUN-2026-08 in linked artifacts).

Appendix (quick math snippets):
- If avg token price compresses by x%, realized revenue delta approximated by: ΔRevenue ≈ MixFactor_hosted * x * HostedShare. Current MixFactor_hosted ~0.85, HostedShare ~0.6 (rough).
- Example: x=0.08 -> ΔRevenue ≈ 0.85 * 0.08 * 0.6 ≈ 0.0408 (4.08%) but further amplified by enterprise churn sensitivity -> model uses 7.2% in mid scenario to reflect churn coupling.
